key_insight: Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 double perovskites show composition-tunable self-trapped exciton emission, where B-site alloying changes the PL energy and polarization anisotropy without strongly affecting absorption.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a route to engineer lead-free optoelectronic nanocrystals with controllable color output and polarization properties by tuning composition rather than changing the host structure.
method: Optical spectroscopy of Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals with Na-to-K B-site alloying
Ab initio calculations of exciton localization, in-gap states, and lattice distortions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a composition-dependent PL shift from about 2.48 to 2.70 eV while absorption near 3.8 eV stays nearly unchanged, and the measured anisotropy matches theory.
watch_item: The reported fingerprints depend on strong exciton-phonon coupling and composition-specific lattice distortions, so device performance may be sensitive to synthesis quality and alloy uniformity.
paper_title: Composition-controlled optical fingerprints and anisotropy of self-trapped excitons in double perovskites
